threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: A dangling reference needs a lifetime the borrow checker cannot see, which in Rust means `unsafe` or foreign code. The package contains no `unsafe` (grep of src/ finds none; the v1 report excludes this class, assurance_report.json:1085-1094) and its only library dependency, transistors, contains none either (grep of transistors/src, 2026-11-24). Only the first half is checked by a tool: the analyzer reads the package's own sources, `closure` is hard-wired to the package (ca-assurance-report/src/lib.rs:117), and no tool reads transistors. The standard library's own `unsafe` is an accepted baseline, not a lane threat. Miri is not run and is unnecessary while the crate is unsafe-free.

threats.name: Out-of-bounds Write
threats.rationale: Safe Rust bounds-checks every slice and Vec write and panics instead of corrupting memory; the package indexes `state[i]`, `inputs[bit_pos]` and slices (combinational.rs:417-420, sequential.rs:296-371), each guarded by a length assert. Out-of-bounds in safe Rust is a panic (rust.indexing-and-slicing-panics), not memory corruption. The exclusion holds only while no `unsafe` is reachable in the package or its dependencies.

threats.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary
threats.rationale: The registry class is narrow: wraparound that yields a wrong buffer size or offset. The package's sizes are `1usize << n` with n <= 16 (combinational.rs:399, cap at :391-395; this was SEC-008, LG01:140) and `Vec::with_capacity` of a length derived from a slice length. Overflow in general (an `u8` sum, shifts, the encoder count that was SEC-007, LG01:128) is the separate lane threat rust.arithmetic-overflow-profile; render this row under its full registry name, never as `integer overflow excluded`.

threats.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
threats.rationale: Per-call work is constant for the two-input gates and linear in the caller's slice for the N-ary gates, mux and encoders; decoder and demux are capped at 16 select bits (MAX_DECODER_WIDTH, combinational.rs:54; SEC-008, LG01:140) and allocate up to 65,536 bytes. The library is NOT allocation-free on the valid path: `validate_bits` builds a `format!("{name}[{i}]")` String for every element before checking it (combinational.rs:76-79), so a valid n-element mux or decoder call allocates O(n) garbage; every call to a gate or block that returns a Vec allocates; sequential state (`CounterState::new(width)`, sequential.rs:396-401) is uncapped. There are no input-length caps on slices (the caller already paid for them). The pure_zero_allocation route is therefore false as written, and the registry discharge needs a microbenchmark of zero allocation, a step-bound proof and an input-bound check; the first cannot pass and the step proof is not live (proof-manifest.json: every steps-bound `not-live`, the front end refuses the source; LG-001 and VER-P048 in VER-BACKLOG.md track the refusals). So only an exclusion route is declared. The v1 report carries an unapproved computed exemption (assurance_report.json:1030, 1209-1214, EXEMPT-CWE-400-NO-STEP-PROOF).

closed_by.detail: Context only, NOT a route (no route fits): not achievable under the registry subset as written: pure_zero_allocation means no allocation, and decoder, demux, encoder, priority_encoder and the register/shift-register/counter functions return `Vec`s, so the package is not zero-allocation by design. Excluding this class would need a new VER15a section 5.5 lane extension for BOUNDED allocation (capped output sizes, nothing proportional to caller input beyond its own length); that extension does not exist and is not planned, and redefining pure_zero_allocation inside an analyzer rule would not be a registry exclusion. Related package fixes: validate_bits builds a String per element on the valid path (LGE-RUST-HARDEN) and sequential widths are uncapped (LGE-DOS-ALL, LGE-RUST-HARDEN).

threats.name: Rejection is a panic, so the consumer's panic strategy decides the outcome
threats.rationale: The error model of the lane is `assert!`: every non-bit, every bad width and every short slice panics (gates.rs:52-57, combinational.rs:67-72, 186-187, 227-240). That is by contract (LG01, LG02 section 7), tested in debug and release. Whether a panic unwinds to a `catch_unwind` or aborts the whole process is set by the FINAL binary's profile (`panic = "abort"` in a dependent's Cargo.toml; profile settings of a dependency crate are ignored), so a caller that passes attacker-chosen integers into a gate can be made to crash its process (CWE-617 reachable assertion, a denial of service in that caller). A panic that unwinds through an `extern "C"` boundary aborts. The package cannot choose the consumer's strategy; the consumer must validate before calling or contain the panic, and every release says so. A `try_*` Result API would be a different contract (LG01) and is not planned.

considered_not_included.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition (Infinite Loop)
considered_not_included.why_not: The only data-dependent loop is the SR-latch settle loop, capped at 10 iterations (sequential.rs:131-145); every other loop is bounded by a slice length or the decoder cap. Non-convergence returns the last state silently, which is a modelling note in LG01, not an infinite loop.

considered_not_included.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
considered_not_included.why_not: Safe Rust frees by ownership; the package has no Rc, no cycle, no `mem::forget` and no static collection. A Vec returned to the caller is the caller's.

considered_not_included.name: Use of Uninitialized Variable
considered_not_included.why_not: Safe Rust refuses to read an uninitialized binding; `MaybeUninit` needs `unsafe`, which is banned (rows CWE-416 and rust.unsafe-not-forbidden).

considered_not_included.name: Unchecked Return Value
considered_not_included.why_not: The gates are pure functions returning u8; ignoring the value is harmless. The only Option is tri_state's and the only Results are the transistor model's, which are unwrapped inside the library (rust.panic-reason-conflation).

considered_not_included.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
considered_not_included.why_not: `assert!` and `format!` use compile-time literal format strings; the caller's integer is an argument, never the format (gates.rs:53-56, combinational.rs:78).

considered_not_included.name: Use of Inherently Dangerous Function
considered_not_included.why_not: Rust has no gets/strcpy family; the dangerous-by-construction items are `unsafe` and `transmute`, covered by the unsafe rows.

considered_not_included.name: Operator Precedence Logic Error
considered_not_included.why_not: Rust comparison operators are non-associative and bitwise operators bind tighter than comparison, so the C pattern `a & b == 1` is a type error here; gates use `==`, `||` on bools only (gates.rs:54).

considered_not_included.name: Use of Incorrect Operator
considered_not_included.why_not: The `=`/`==` confusion does not compile in an `if`/`assert!` condition (assignment is not a bool) and `&&`/`&` confusion is type-checked on u8 vs bool.

considered_not_included.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
considered_not_included.why_not: Rust has no implicit numeric conversion; every conversion is an explicit `as`, handled by rust.lossy-as-casts and CWE-704.

considered_not_included.name: Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound)
considered_not_included.why_not: Folded into rust.arithmetic-overflow-profile (CWE-128); the only subtractions are `n - 1` after `n >= 2` and `width - 1` after `width >= 1`.

considered_not_included.name: Off-by-one Error
considered_not_included.why_not: Folded into rust.indexing-and-slicing-panics: an off-by-one index panics rather than corrupting memory.

considered_not_included.name: Divide By Zero
considered_not_included.why_not: The only division is `n / 2` by a literal (combinational.rs:259); there is no caller-controlled divisor.

considered_not_included.name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
considered_not_included.why_not: Safe Rust has no undefined behaviour; the behaviour of `as` and overflow is specified (and profile-dependent, which is rust.arithmetic-overflow-profile).

considered_not_included.name: Numeric Range Comparison Without Minimum Check
considered_not_included.why_not: Parameters are unsigned `u8`; the check `value == 0 || value == 1` is exact on the whole domain (gates.rs:54).

considered_not_included.name: Incorrect Short Circuit Evaluation
considered_not_included.why_not: Folded into CWE-20: every gate validates both arguments before computing (gates.rs:137-138), pinned by the all-U8x all-U8 Warrant claims.

considered_not_included.name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
considered_not_included.why_not: A wrong arity is a compile error in Rust; there are no variadics.

considered_not_included.name: Incorrect Bitwise Shift of Integer
considered_not_included.why_not: Folded into rust.arithmetic-overflow-profile; the only shifts are `1usize << n` with n <= 16 and `(x >> k) & 1` with k < 64.

considered_not_included.name: Uncaught Exception
considered_not_included.why_not: Folded into rust.panic-as-error-model (CWE-617): a Rust panic is the language's analogue and is the same row.

considered_not_included.name: Improper Initialization
considered_not_included.why_not: Every struct is built by a constructor or `Default` with explicit values (sequential.rs:55-65, 396-402); FlipFlopState's public fields are rust.public-state-fields.

considered_not_included.name: Missing Synchronization
considered_not_included.why_not: Send/Sync: every public type is plain data (u8 fields, Vec<u8>); there is no interior mutability, no static and no unsafe impl Send/Sync, so the compiler's auto traits are sound by construction.

considered_not_included.name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
considered_not_included.why_not: .cargo/config.toml (it sets only a Windows linker, .cargo/config.toml:1-2) and RUSTFLAGS/CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS in a consumer or CI environment can change overflow checks, panic strategy or lints without any package file changing; no tool inspects them. Consumer-side; see rust.panic-as-error-model and rust.profile-dependent-behaviour.

considered_not_included.why_not: Not a weakness class a gate package is exposed to; unreachable items are warned by rustc and clippy under -D warnings in CI.
